evidence: At 390x844 mobile viewport with visibility filtering (computed display/visibility checked, zero-size elements excluded): /app/log has 180 visible interactive elements, 81 below 44px — 'Open daily review' 32x32 @(302,12), 'Open user settings menu' 32x32 @(342,12), filter pills All 39x28 / Favorites 75x28 / Dislikes 66x28 / Recently used 101x28 (all 28px tall with only 8px gaps), and ~50 'Choose [food]' buttons at 40x40. /app/fitness has 12 small targets ('View full day' 308x36, 'Edit routine' 114x32, 'Open workouts' 134x32). /app/dashboard has 7 (32x32 header icons, 42x42 Search/Notifications). Artifact checks: the 32x32 icons live in the mobile-only header (md:hidden sticky top-0) and are in-viewport; elementFromPoint at their centers returns the elements themselves; no padding/pseudo-element extends the hit area (probe 6px outside the rect misses; pills are px-3 py-1.5 text-xs = full 28px height, no ::before/::after content); a real Playwright tap() on the 28px-tall Favorites pill toggled its selected class (bg-primary-50 -> bg-primary-600 text-white), proving these are live sub-44px controls. reason: The undersized touch targets are real, visible, in-viewport, live interactive elements whose effective hit areas equal their sub-44px visual rects — not display:none artifacts or elements with extended tap areas. Multiple independent reviewer measurements match my own pixel-for-pixel.
qualifier: Severity is concentrated on /app/log (81 small targets incl. 28px-tall filter pills and 40x40 choose buttons) and /app/fitness (12); /app/dashboard is comparatively mild (7, mostly the shared 32x32 header icons and 42x42 buttons that miss the bar by 2px).

evidence: Tested live app at 390x844 via Playwright on /app/dashboard, /app/settings, /app/grocery-list. (1) The desktop sidebar is <aside class="relative hidden shrink-0 ... md:flex md:flex-col ..."> with computed display:none, visibility:visible on mobile — the Tailwind hidden/md:flex responsive pattern. All 14 sidebar links/buttons (Dashboard, Daily Review, Log Meal, Coach, Workouts, Collapse menu, etc.) report 0x0 via getBoundingClientRect solely because they sit inside this display:none subtree; every one has offsetParent === null and a display:none ancestor. Per-route totals: 15 of ~74 a/button elements are 0x0, and all 15 are the hidden sidebar — including on /app/grocery-list, where A11 attributed 0x0 to filter/qty buttons (those measure normally; e.g. 'Mark all shopped' 168x72, 'Clear list' 124x74, 'Add item' 964x48). (2) Keyboard test: pressed Tab 40 times on each of the 3 routes and recorded document.activeElement rects — 0 zero-size tab stops on all routes; focus never lands on any sidebar element, refuting A08-F3's 'trap tabs' claim. Dashboard tab order goes header (77x28 FuelWell home, 32x32 icons) → content cards → bottom nav. (3) Accessibility tree (ariaSnapshot): contains no 'Collapse menu', no 'Workouts', no sidebar entries; the only 'Recovery' match is the visible dashboard card 'Recovery Checklist incomplete'. (4) A real mobile nav exists: navigation aria-label='Mobile navigation', 390x70 fixed bottom bar with 6 visible links (Home/Log/Coach/Move/Groceries/Review) at 65x45–65x49, present in tab order and a11y tree.
reason: The 0x0 readings are the standard getBoundingClientRect artifact of measuring display:none elements. The sidebar is already properly hidden on mobile exactly as the cluster's proposed fix demands (display:none removes it from rendering, tab order, AND the accessibility tree — no aria-hidden needed), and a dedicated visible mobile bottom nav replaces it. Reviewers inspected raw DOM dimensions without checking computed display or actual focusability; every member finding I traced (A06-F2, A08-F3, A11-F3/F8, A12-F1/F3, A13-F4, A17-F1) reduces to this same artifact. No user on a mobile viewport can encounter invisible-but-focusable nav elements.

evidence: Tested live at localhost:3000, 390x844 mobile viewport (Playwright/Chromium). (1) /signup: email+password inputs never set aria-invalid (stays null after invalid input, after blur, and after submit); border color unchanged rgb(214,240,232) with 'invalid-email' value; zero [role=alert] or error-text elements in DOM in any state; no required asterisks (labels are just 'Email','Password'). HOWEVER inputs DO have required=true, password minlength=8, form is not novalidate — empty submit is blocked by native HTML5 validation (validationMessage 'Please fill out this field.', browser focuses first invalid field, URL stays /signup), so 'button click completes silently' (A19-F6) is a tooling artifact: real users get native bubbles. (2) /app/log food picker: amount input has min=0 max='' no step; empty and 0g are blocked only by silently disabling 'Add to Breakfast' (verified disabled at ''/0, enabled at 150) with no message explaining why; NO upper limit — 999999g accepted, toast 'Chicken breast, grilled (999999 g) added to breakfast.', dashboard then shows '1649998 kcal' with no warning. (3) /app/log custom meal form ('Add your own meal'): 7 visible inputs, all required=false, maxLength=-1, macro inputs min=0 max=''; clicking 'Add to Breakfast' with the form empty is a silent no-op — 0 error elements, 0 toasts, form stays open; 190-char name with emoji accepted with no counter/limit. (4) /app/onboarding: no asterisks, 0 occurrences of 'required', 0 role=alert; required steps (Birthday) gate progression by silently disabling Next with no explanatory text; optional name step advances empty. (5) /app/progress 'Today's weight' input is type=text inputmode=decimal, accepts 'abc' and '99999' with zero error feedback (preview-only per its own label). (6) /app/profile: read-only summary page, no visible form fields, 0 required marks, 0 role=alert.
reason: The core defect pattern is real and observed first-hand: the app has no custom inline-validation layer anywhere — aria-invalid is never set, no error text/red borders/role=alert exist in any tested form state, no required-field indication exists, and numeric inputs have no sane upper limits (999999g portion logged producing a 1,649,998 kcal day with a success toast). Empty-submit protection exists only as silent mechanisms (native browser bubbles on /signup, silently disabled buttons on /app/log and onboarding) that give no accessible or explanatory feedback, and the custom-meal form fails fully silently on empty submit.
qualifier: Partially overstated for /signup: A19-F6's 'empty form submission produces 0 error messages / completes silently' is a headless-DOM artifact — inputs are required and the form is not novalidate, so real browsers block submit and show native validation bubbles (not DOM elements). The genuine gap on /signup is absence of custom/inline/accessible feedback (aria-invalid, error text, red border), not absence of all validation. Also A01-F13's 0g-meal fear is mitigated: the Add button is disabled at 0g/empty — the defect there is the unexplained disabled state and the missing upper limit, not 0g acceptance. A15-F10's speculation is confirmed via the log portion path (999999g accepted).

Only the "too subtle" half reproduces. The "missing / outline=0px" half is refuted: every one of 48+ real keyboard Tab stops measured across /app/dashboard, /app/log, /app/recipes, /app/coach and /preview showed a 2-3px solid outline with :focus-visible matching. The 0px/transparent readings in A19-F14, A18-F1, A08-F5, A09-F6 and A06-F1 are tooling artifacts (styles read after blur, or on click/script focus where the app's :focus-visible rule correctly does not fire).
evidence: Playwright, real keyboard.press("Tab"), computed styles read on document.activeElement WHILE focused, 1280x800: /app/dashboard Tab3 "Dashboard" nav link: outline "3px solid oklab(0.669282 -0.127436 0.029258 / 0.5)", focusVisible=true; /app/log Tab1 "High protein" pill: "2px solid oklab(... / 0.5)" offset 2px (directly contradicting A19-F14's "outline=0px, boxShadow transparent" and A08-F5's "outlineStyle none" on the same button); /app/coach nav links 3px solid (contradicting A09-F6's "solid 0px"); text inputs get full-opacity "2px solid rgb(21,145,108)". Pixel sampling of screenshots: on /app/log the rendered ring is rgb(87,183,154) on white = 2.43:1 contrast (below WCAG 2.2's 3:1 non-text minimum); on /preview (dark hub) the ring renders rgb(26,101,79) on rgb(24,24,24) = 1.92:1 — visually a faint dark-green ring on near-black, confirmed in clipped screenshot. On light surfaces the ring is clearly visible to the eye (screenshots focus-log-btn.png, focus-dash-nav.png in scratchpad); on dark surfaces it is genuinely hard to see.
reason: The cluster's core claim of missing focus indicators does not reproduce — a global :focus-visible outline fires on every element under real keyboard navigation, and the many 0px readings came from measuring blurred or click-focused elements. However, the outline color uses the primary green at 50% alpha, and measured rendered contrast is 2.43:1 against light surfaces and 1.92:1 against the dark /preview background — below the 3:1 non-text contrast threshold, so the "too subtle" complaints (A02-F4, A09-F6, A13-F2 substance) are legitimate, especially on dark backgrounds. The proposed fix (single adequate-contrast :focus-visible token for light and dark surfaces) targets a real defect.
affected_locations: /preview (nav links, ring contrast 1.92:1 on dark background — worst case)

reason: The core defect is real and observed first-hand on 6 of 7 routes checked: cal/kcal/calories/CAL are used interchangeably (often three variants on a single page), thousands separators are applied inconsistently to same-magnitude numbers on the same page, and gram values mix "Xg" and "X g" spacing within one view. qualifier: Partially overstated by reviewers in two respects: the "30gCarb"/"102gPro" camelCase formats (A08-F9/F14) do not exist visually — they are textContent tooling artifacts of a number and its label on separate lines; and "850kcal"/"483kcal" are number+unit spans separated by a 4px CSS margin, i.e. a deliberate big-number/small-unit style rather than a literal missing space, though it still contrasts with plain "1883 kcal" / "1,400 kcal" text on the same pages.

Only the route-transition sub-claim (A12-F12) reproduced, and only on slow networks: routes other than /app/dashboard lack loading.tsx, so under emulated slow-3G a tap on a nav link leaves the old page visible with zero pending indicators for ~1.6s. The cluster's headline claims are refuted: /app/recipes is NOT blank (8 recipe headings in DOM at domcontentloaded, 79,873-char body, 0 data fetches — recipes are a static in-memory array, fully SSR'd); food search is synchronous local lookup (55 results in 67ms, 0 network requests, so a fetch spinner is inapplicable); coach DOES show a 'Working...' processing indicator with animated dots 350ms after send; dashboard already has a full skeleton loading.tsx; no fetch-driven layout shift observed. The proposed fix theme ('add spinners to search/recipes/coach fetches') targets fetches that do not exist — the only actionable fix is adding loading.tsx (or a transition indicator) to non-dashboard routes.

evidence: Audited every button/a/[role=button] on /app/dashboard, /app/log, /app/coach, /app/daily-review at 390x844 mobile with full accessible-name computation (aria-label, aria-labelledby, text, title, svg title, img alt) plus a Playwright ariaSnapshot of the real accessibility tree. Results: (1) Zero unnamed interactive elements on all four routes (dashboard 47 elements, log 198, coach 35, daily-review 53). (2) The button A03-F1 calls unlabeled has aria-label="Open user settings menu" — the reviewers quoted its own aria-label while claiming it has none; their check read textContent, not the accessible name. (3) Coach send button (A05-F14, A15-F16): aria-label="Send", 48x48px; ariaSnapshot shows `button "Send" [disabled]`. A15's own evidence even printed the name "Send". (4) Dashboard icons (A06-F10, A20-F6): aria-label="Search" (42x42), "Notifications" (42x42), "Open user settings menu", "Open daily review" — A06's "0 of 10 icons have aria-label" is false; they likely sampled SVG child nodes instead of parent buttons. (5) Health Score "Details" (A09-F7) is an <a> with visible text "Details" — its accessible name; aria-label absent on a text link is not a defect. (6) Bottom nav (A01-F16): links Home/Log/Coach/Move/Groceries/Review each render a VISIBLE 11px text label (measured spans e.g. "Home" 27.95x11px, display:block, no clip/hidden) below the icon, plus accessible names in the AX tree. (7) Meal buttons (A01-F5) are native <button> elements — implicit role=button; getAttribute("role")===null is a tooling artifact, explicit role attr is unnecessary. (8) Daily-review expanders (A18-F21): all 9 aria-expanded buttons have accessible names ("Collapse section", "Expand", "Hide", or aria-labels); "only 2 of 9 have aria-label" is technically true but the other 7 are named via text content, which is the correct pattern. (9) /app/log icon buttons: all 114 icon-only buttons named ("Like this", "Not for me", "Choose Chicken breast, grilled", "Edit Greek yogurt with berries", "Close ingredient drawer").
reason: The cluster's core claim — icon-only controls with no accessible name — does not exist anywhere on the cited routes. Reviewers systematically confused empty textContent with "no accessible name" and ignored aria-label attributes (several findings literally quote the aria-label they claim is missing). The nav-label sub-claim is also false: bottom-nav icons have visible 11px text labels. The only kernel of truth is a naming-quality nit, not a defect matching this cluster: two daily-review expanders use generic names ("Expand", "Hide") that don't identify which section they control, and A15-F13's complaint is about label specificity for voice control, not missing labels. The proposed fix theme (add aria-labels and visible nav text labels) is already implemented in the app.
qualifier: Minor residual observation, outside the cluster's defect definition: on /app/daily-review a few expander buttons are named generically ("Expand", "Hide") without identifying their section, which could be improved for voice-control disambiguation — but every control has a valid accessible name.

Partially. Button/chip padding variance and cross-page section-gap variance are real; but the cluster's headline evidence (A14-F13 negative -177px gap / "sections overlap" on Daily Review) is REFUTED — it is a tooling artifact from measuring nested <section> elements as siblings. True sibling sections on every measured page have perfectly consistent gaps within the page.
evidence: Measured at 1280x800 via Playwright against http://localhost:3000. (1) Daily Review section gaps: the 4 true sibling sections inside `.fw-page-inner.space-y-7` sit at y 141-671, 699-1243, 1271-1591, 1619-2782 → gaps exactly [28, 28, 28]. No overlap; the reported -177px came from counting a nested `SECTION.grid.gap-3` (top 494, inside the first card at 141-671) as a sibling. (2) Dashboard: 5 sibling sections in `.fw-page-inner.space-y-6` → gaps [24, 24, 24, 24] (consistent, matching A05-F10's own observation). (3) /app/nutrition: 5 sibling sections → gaps [16, 16, 16, 16]; marginBottom values across all visible main div/section elements are {0px:72, 16px:10, 10px:4, 20px:2, 12px:2} — NOT the [0, 16, 24, 32, auto] A10-F4 reported, and all on Tailwind's 2px sub-grid. (4) A08-F4 reproduced literally: dashboard has exactly 7 buttons with exactly 3 unique paddings — '0px' (5 fixed-size circular icon buttons, 39-44px squares), '12px 24px' ('Find meals that fit' pill, 188x44), '10px 16px' ('Open meal breakdown' row button, 381x42) — though these are different component types, not "similar-looking". (5) Genuine same-component inconsistency on /app/log: two adjacent filter-chip groups 50px apart use different chip specs — recipe-filter chips ('High protein', 'Low carb', 'Low fat', 'Vegan'): padding 6px 14px, font 14px, height 34px vs custom-food chips ('All', 'Favorites', 'Dislikes', 'Recently used'): padding 6px 12px, font 12px, height 28px; plus 10 unique button padding values total on that page. (6) Cross-page top-level rhythm varies: 28px (daily-review) vs 24px (dashboard) vs 16px (nutrition card stack).
reason: Partially reproduced. The literal representative evidence for button padding (A08-F4: 7 buttons, 3 paddings '0px'/'12px 24px'/'10px 16px') reproduced exactly, and there is a genuine visible inconsistency between two nearly identical filter-chip groups on /app/log plus cross-page section-gap variance (28/24/16px). However the highest-severity representative claim — negative -177px gap / overlapping sections on Daily Review (A14-F13) — is refuted: it results from treating nested sections as siblings; actual sibling gaps are a perfectly uniform 28px, and within-page section rhythm is internally consistent on every page measured. The proposed fix theme's "fix the negative-gap overlap on Daily Review" targets a non-existent defect; the legitimate remaining scope is chip/button padding tokens and cross-page gap normalization.
